glosses: imprint, impress

examples.text: отпеча́ток па́льца

glosses: изображение, оставшееся на чём-либо от надавливания другого предмета; след

examples.text: С каждым шагом всё яснее становились отпечатки лап медведя.
Копировальная бумага не вечна: чем больше копий сделано с её помощью, тем меньше остается на ней краски и тем более бледным становится отпечаток.
― Ой, у тебя на щеке отпечаток подушки!

glosses: фотографический снимок, полученный посредством печати с негатива

examples.text: Наиболее простой путь расцвечивания снимков состоит в переводе черно-белого негатива в цветной отпечаток методом тоноразделения.

glosses: перен. признак как результат влияния какой-либо среды, событий и т. п.

examples.text: На ней лежал отпечаток той школы, в которой она довершила светское воспитание, того круга, в котором жила с малолетства.

Зато нравом он походил на отца; и несхожее с отцовским лицо носило отпечаток отцовского выражения, и руки имел он узловатые, и впалую грудь, как старик Аратов, которого, впрочем, едва ли следует называть стариком, так как он и до пятидесяти лет не дотянул.
Хотя он из старой дворянской семьи, но его узкая профессия наложила на него некоторый отпечаток.
Как и ожидалось, послание носило на себе отпечаток того обстоятельства, что оно произносилось в год выборов в Думу и за год до президентских выборов.

glosses: An impression; the mark left behind by printing something.

examples.text: The day left an imprint in my mind.
It was the moment everyone knew the Champions League trophy was on its way back to the Bernabéu and, once again, that the four-times Ballon d’Or winner had left his imprint on another final.

glosses: The name and details of a publisher or printer, as printed in a book etc.; a publishing house.

examples.text: From their Belmont Avenue address they issued such memorable titles as I Peddle Jazz, Camera Bait, Our Flesh Was Cheap, Lesbian Twins, and His Sex, His Problem under at least four different imprints—Saber, Fabian, Vega, and National Library Books.

glosses: A distinctive marking, symbol or logo.

examples.text: The shirts bore the company imprint on the right sleeve.

glosses: To leave a print, impression, image, etc.

examples.text: For a fee, they can imprint the envelopes with a monogram.

For though a Child quickly aſſent to this Propoſition, That an Apple is not Fire; when, by familiar Acquaintance, he has got the Idea's of thoſe two different things diſtinctly imprinted on his Mind, and has learnt that the names Apple and Fire ſtand for them; yet it will be ſome years after, perhaps, before the ſame Child will aſſent to this Propoſition, That it is impoſſible for the ſame thing to be, and not to be.
Him great in peace and wealth fair Deva knows; / For ſhe amidſt his ſpacious meadows flows; / Inclines her urn upon his fatten'd lands; / And ſees his num'rous herd imprint her ſands.
Nature imprints upon whate'er we ſee / That has a heart and life in it, be free; [...]

glosses: To learn something indelibly at a particular stage of life, such as who one's parents are.

examples.text: That is, by way of this initial imprinting the young animal becomes a socialized member of its species. Animals misimprinted to other species show a variety of abnormal social behaviors as adults.

glosses: To mark a gene as being from a particular parent so that only one of the two copies of the gene is expressed.
To affect (someone) strongly and often favourably.

examples.text: You impressed me with your command of Urdu.
Mr. Campion appeared suitably impressed and she warmed to him. He was very easy to talk to with those long clown lines in his pale face, a natural goon, born rather too early she suspected.
Okay, so you're a rocket scientist / That don't impress me much

glosses: To make an impression, to be impressive.

examples.text: Henderson impressed in his first game as captain.

Manchester United's Tom Cleverley impressed on his first competitive start and Lampard demonstrated his continued worth at international level in a performance that was little more than a stroll once England swiftly exerted their obvious authority.

glosses: To produce a vivid impression of (something).

examples.text: That first view of the Eiger impressed itself on my mind.

glosses: To mark or stamp (something) using pressure.

examples.text: We impressed our footprints in the wet cement.

glosses: To produce (a mark, stamp, image, etc.); to imprint (a mark or figure upon something).
To fix deeply in the mind; to present forcibly to the attention, etc.; to imprint; to inculcate.

examples.text: impress the motives and methods of persuasion upon our own hearts, till we feel the force and power of them.

glosses: To compel (someone) to serve in a military force.

examples.text: The press gang used to impress people into the Navy.

glosses: To seize or confiscate (property) by force.

examples.text: The liner was impressed as a troop carrier.
the second £5,000 imprest for the service of the sick and wounded prisoners

glosses: The act of impressing.
An impression; an impressed image or copy of something.

examples.text: This weak impress of love is as a figure / Trenched in ice.
We know that you were pressed for money, that you took an impress of the keys which your brother held […]

glosses: A stamp or seal used to make an impression.
An impression on the mind, imagination etc.

examples.text: Such admonitions, in the English of the Authorized Version, left an indelible impress on imaginations nurtured on the Bible […]

glosses: Characteristic; mark of distinction; stamp.

examples.text: we have God surveying the works of the creation, and leaving this general impress or character upon them

As he himself [Sir Nigel Gresley] would doubtless have wished, he died in harness; only a few weeks previously he had been present at the first public view of his latest design, the Bantam Cock, which, like most of his products, bore all over it the impress of his personality.

glosses: A heraldic device; an impresa.

examples.text: It commonly occurred that Knights who , on entering the Lists , wished to conceal their identity , would assume a Device with an allusive Motto , which was designated an IMPRESS
To describe […] emblazon'd Shields, / Impreses quaint.

glosses: The act of impressing, or taking by force for the public service; compulsion to serve; also, that which is impressed.

examples.text: Why such impress of shipwrights?

glosses: Plural 1: das Abdrücken eines härteren Gegenstandes in einen weicheren

examples.text: Schon wieder schwarze Abdrücke auf dem Teppich.
„An der Stelle, wo früher der Tisch gestanden hat, ist jetzt kein Tisch mehr, aber dort, wo seine Beine waren, sieht man immer noch die vier Abdrücke im Fußboden.“

„Der Fußboden war dicht besät mit den Abdrücken eines nackten Fußes – er war klar umrissen und gut abgezeichnet, vollendet in seiner Form, aber dieser Fuß war kaum halb so groß wie der eines normalen Mannes.“

„Sie waren höchst erstaunt, als sie lasen, daß es auf Steinen Abdrücke von Libellen, von Vogelfüßen gibt; und nachdem sie in einem Band von Rorets Handbuch geblättert hatten, begannen sie, nach Fossilien zu suchen.“

glosses: Plural 2: das Abdrucken eines Druckkörpers oder einer Druckform (z. B. auf einen zu bedruckenden Stoff)

examples.text: Die Abdrucke müssen noch sortiert werden.

glosses: nur Singular: das Abdrucken z. B. eines Bildes in einem Printmedium

examples.text: Der Abdruck dieses Fotos ist nicht gestattet.
